note: Colleague status update on crossarm capitalization and vehicle idling, with an open ask back to Chuck. Internal but substantive.

body.content:
Chuck, a few update points:

Maintenance Crossarm Capitalization:

  * 2025 Breakdown and preventive maintenance crossarm usage was $6.4M in 2025
  * Confirmed that all other crossarm applications (new business, reliability, etc.) are currently capitalized.
  * Initial opinion from property accounting is that the change is appropriate, but it will require CAVE determination, regulatory input, and management review to determine implementation timing.
  * Initial draft of hypothesis/charter document developed. If we capitalize breakdown and preventive maintenance crossarms, we can reduce O&M by $6.4 in preventive and breakdown distribution maintenance budgets, and increase capital investment by that amount.
  * Partially developed draft sent to Nanique Castro with additional questions about the CAVE process, and comparisons to other projects that passed through the process.
  * The additional questions are to determine if the materiality level and impacts are similar to other mid-GRC-cycle changes that were pursued - like the change of how underground locates were being charged (direct vs overhead allocations)

Vehicle Idling:

  * Q and I Performed initial analysis of idling data, but require additional data to size the opportunity and develop the hypothesis.
  * Sent data request to Julian Kung on Wed, 7/29/2026, requested due date of Friday, 8/7/2026 from Wil Nevarez,and provided SCE with guidance on which data items were the highest priorities. Wil Nevares indicated that this due date may not be achievable.
  * Chuck - Need to check if we have set up Wil with access to the sharing team folder.
  * Held transition meeting with Wil Nevarez (picking up the project) and Julian Kung
  * As soon as we get the data, we will analyze and develop the Hypothesis.
  * If we cannot get the data timely, we may need to develop a low to medium confidence estimate for a draft Hypothesis target for 8/12/2026. It would likely need to be stated in ranges - if we can reduce idle by 10%, 15%... on XXX set of vehicles, then we can save $WWW, $YYY, $ZZZ in distribution fuel O&M (and Capital depending on the allocations).
  * Total 2025 idling > 2 minutes is 1.44M hours with an estimated idling fuel consumption of 1M gallons across all distribution vehicle and fuel types.
  * At the current $4/gallon estimate in the Samsara data, this represents total annual idling cost of $4M (800k O&M at an 80/20 Capital/O&M split) subject to change based on the more detailed data request)
  * The opportunity will be dependent on the fraction of addressable idle, but will be much less than the total $4M (Cap + O&M) per year.
  * Light duty pickup trucks, vans, cars, and SUVs are significant contributors to the total idling > 2 minutes, and represent nearly half of the total idling > 2 minutes. Most idling events are brief (long right tailed distribution from shortest to longest idle times)

Please let me know if you need additional information. Generally we are awaiting either review/comments from Nanique on XARMs or Data on idling at this time, and will act quickly as soon as we get the docs and data back.

Shawn
